title: Some allow modes one and two, but reject mode three (image alone as per-se adored thing)
source_text: VII. Alii ergo docent imagines non tantum primo modo jam dicto, sed etiam secundo licite coli posse; nempe non solum exemplar coram imagine posse adorari, sed adoranti licere adorationem suam referre atque terminare ad exemplar & imaginem simul, unum, scilicet, objectum totale ex duobus hisce mente conficiendo. Sed rejiciunt, tanquam illicitum, tertium modum adorationis, in quo imago sola est res per se adorata, quamvis adoretur propter exemplar, quod est ratio adorationis illius.
pass_a_gloss: Others therefore teach that images can lawfully be cultivated not only in the first mode already stated, but also in the second; namely that not only can the exemplar be adored before the image, but it is lawful for the adorer to refer and terminate his adoration to exemplar and image together, composing, namely, one total object from these two with the mind. But they reject, as illicit, the third mode of adoration, in which the image alone is the thing adored per se, although it is adored on account of the exemplar, which is the reason of that adoration.
pass_b_english: Middle party: modes one and two are licit—adoration may terminate on exemplar-plus-image as one total object.
Mode three (image alone as the per-se adored thing) they brand illicit, even when the exemplar is the reason.
